cards.text: Jesus has just fed a crowd of about five thousand men, besides women and children (Matthew 14:21). Right away, He makes the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side. Then He sends the crowds away.

cards.question: Once the crowds are gone, Jesus goes up on the mountain by Himself. What for?

cards.text: Evening comes, and Jesus is up there alone. Meanwhile the boat is already far from land, getting beaten by the waves.

cards.question: The disciples' boat is getting beaten by the waves because the ___ is against it.

cards.text: Then, during the fourth watch of the night, Jesus heads out to the boat. And this part, friend? You're gonna want to sit down.

cards.question: During the fourth watch of the night, how does Jesus get out to the disciples' boat?

cards.text: The disciples see Him walking on the sea, and they are TERRIFIED. Honestly, I'd scream too, and I scream when an oven timer goes off that I forgot I set.

cards.question: The terrified disciples cry out in fear. What do they think Jesus is?
Jesus waits until the storm calms down before He says anything to the frightened disciples.

cards.text: Jesus speaks up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.” Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, calls back, “Lord, if it is You,” and asks for something WILD.

cards.question: Out on the stormy sea, what does Peter ask Jesus to do?

answers.text: Command him to come on the water

cards.text: Jesus answers with one word: “Come.” So Peter gets down out of the boat.

cards.question: After Peter gets down out of the boat, he walks on the water and comes toward Jesus.

cards.text: Peter is WALKING. ON. WATER. Friend, I'm attached to a gold base and I STILL trip over my own mixing bowls.
Peter's out on the water, heading toward Jesus. Then he notices what's going on around him.

cards.question: Out on the water, Peter sees something, gets afraid and begins to sink. What does he see?

cards.text: Peter starts to sink and cries out, “Lord, save me!” Three words, no speech, which is exactly how I yell when a tray of cookies slides off the counter.

cards.question: As Peter sinks, Jesus ___ reaches out His hand and takes hold of him.

cards.text: Jesus tells him, “You of little faith,” and asks, “why did you doubt?” I bet Peter is very wet and very quiet right about now.

cards.question: Jesus and Peter are still out on the sea. When does the wind finally die down?

answers.text: When they climb back into the boat
When Peter cries out for help
When Jesus speaks to the wind

cards.question: The wind dies down, and everyone in the boat ___ Jesus, saying He is truly the ___ of God.

cards.text: They cross over and land at Gennesaret, and the men there recognize Jesus. Friend, nobody ever recognizes me, and I've got a mustache you can see from space.

cards.question: Once the men of Gennesaret recognize Jesus, what do they do?

answers.text: Send word to all the surrounding region
Ask Him to leave their region
Keep His visit a quiet secret

cards.text: And here they come. People bring all the sick to Him.

cards.question: In Gennesaret, what do the people beg Jesus to let them do?

answers.text: Just touch the fringe of His cloak
Hear Him teach beside the sea

cards.question: In Gennesaret, only some of the people who touched Jesus were healed.

findings.problem: The setup line "You're gonna want to sit down" tells the baker that something astonishing is coming. That rules out the ordinary wrong answer "In a borrowed boat" on card 6 before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says Peter "asks for something WILD." That rules out the plain wrong answer "Climb up into the boat" on card 11, which leaves the baker only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats what card 13 already told: Peter walks on the water (Matthew 14:29). It adds a joke but doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: In the second blank, the wrong word "Lamb" gives "truly the Lamb of God." That is a real title of Jesus (John 1:29), and Papa Dorin's backstory leans on it. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 4 of the 7 choice cards in each stop, and stop 1 has only one fill in the blank. Both stops also open the same way: multiple choice, then fill in the blank, then multiple choice.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
